name: Kolvane Transit Six-Panel Cap
description:
A structured six-panel cap in faded slate-grey synth-canvas with a pre-curved brim coated in rubberized waterproofing. The Kolvane wordmark is embroidered in muted copper thread above the brow. The sweatband is moisture-wicking mesh with a small neural-port relief notch cut into the rear band — a practical detail that made Kolvane the default cap brand for augmented transit workers across Circuit.

Sizing runs via an internal dial adjuster at the back. Most worn examples show brim grease and salt-bleached panels from years of outdoor platform work.
functionality: Waterproof brim deflects acid-rain drizzle; neural-port relief notch accommodates standard single-port and dual-port BCI hardware without pressure points. UV-resistant fabric rated for extended outdoor platform exposure.
what_it_says: You clock in, you do the job, and you've been doing it long enough that your gear knows your hardware.
story_hooks: Kolvane caps have been turning up with a counterfeit label hiding a micro-transmitter in the brim — someone is tracking transit workers.
A limited run of caps was accidentally dyed with a pigment that reacts to a specific airborne toxin, turning red — workers have been quietly hoarding them.
The original Kolvane family is trying to reclaim their brand name from the distributor that bought it out, and they need proof of original production.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn, utilitarian six-panel cap with a structured crown and pre-curved brim. The faded slate-grey fabric has a softened, lived-in appearance typical of daily transit worker use. The silhouette reads as classic workwear, slightly oversized in the crown to accommodate neural ports and augmentation hardware.
physical_description.fit: Adjustable via internal dial mechanism at rear; fits snug but not restrictive. The neural-port relief notch at the back band allows clearance for subcutaneous or port-based augmentation without pressure points. Crown sits comfortably above augmented ocular implants.
physical_description.primary_material: Faded synth-canvas in slate-grey; rubberized waterproof coating on the brim; moisture-wicking mesh sweatband interior.
physical_description.texture: Canvas has a soft, broken-in nap from repeated wear and washing. Brim feels slightly tacky from waterproofing. Embroidery thread is raised and tactile. Sweatband is breathable mesh with a slight stretch.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded slate-grey primary; muted copper-thread embroidery for Kolvane wordmark above brow; darker salt stains and grease marks concentrated at brim edges and crown creases.
physical_description.closures: Dial adjuster mechanism at rear band; no traditional fasteners—friction-fit adjustment.
distinctive_features: Pre-curved brim with rubberized waterproof coating
Neural-port relief notch cut into rear sweatband
Kolvane wordmark in copper thread embroidery
Visible salt bleaching and platform-work patina
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional workwear; affordable, durable, unglamorous. Signals working-class transit labor and augmentation accessibility.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by metro operators, platform workers, Iowan Behemoth maintenance crews, and augmented transit personnel across the Circuit. The neural-port notch is a status marker—signals regular augmentation use without pretense. Kolvane is the street-level choice for people who work outdoors in all weather.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn and patinated. Brim edges show salt bloom and grease stains. Fabric is softened and slightly faded. Sweatband may show discoloration. Stitching remains intact. Embroidery is dulled but readable. Often paired with other worn workwear.

The brim shows visible salt stains and grease patina. The neural-port notch is subtly visible at the rear band. Copper embroidery thread catches cold light above the brow.
